§6Petroleum Gas§f

§aThe least common refinery output but the most versatile. Polymer, bakelite, fuel, fracking, it does everything.§f

Petroleum Gas is a flammable gas from the §bOil Refinery§f. Every §e1,000mB§f of hot crude oil yields only §e100mB§f of it, but its uses are everywhere.

§6Production§f:
§b• Oil Refinery§f: §e100mB§f per §e1,000mB§f hot crude oil.
§b• Cracking Tower§f: Crack §bNatural Gas§f, §bKerosene§f, §bDiesel§f, §bBTX§f, §bIndustrial Oil§f, or §bCrude Oil§f.
§b• Hydrotreater§f: §bNatural Gas§f → §e800mB§f Petroleum Gas.

§6Key Uses§f:
§b• Polymer§f: §e500mB§f + Coal Powder + Fluorite → §e1× Polymer Bar§f.
§b• Bakelite§f: §e500mB§f + §e500mB§f Aromatic Hydrocarbons → §e1× Bakelite Bar§f.
§b• LPG§f: §e2,000mB§f → §e1,000mB§f LPG in a §bCompressor§f.
§b• Fracking Solution§f: §e100mB§f + §e900mB§f Sulfuric Acid.
§b• Nitroglycerin§f: §e1,000mB§f + Nitric Acid.

Also found in §bGas Shale§f blocks (§e250mB§f each) above oil deposits.

§ePS:§f Burns at §e1.65 MTU§f and §e2.47 MHE§f per bucket. Decent fuel, but its chemical uses are way more valuable.
